newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech trade deficit meeting postponed - Industry Min.
newsitem.headline: Czech trade deficit meeting postponed - Industry Min.

text.p: A meeting of Czech economic ministers and central bank Governor Josef Tosovsky over the spiralling trade deficit has been postponed, Industry and Trade Ministry spokesman Miroslav Konvalina said on Monday.
Konvalina gave no new date for the meeting, which had been scheduled for October 8.
"The meeting has been postponed," Konvalina said, adding that Tuesday's parliamentary session was the reason for the postponement.

The session has long been scheduled. However, the cabinet called a hastily-announced meeting for Monday to discuss relations between the minority government of Vaclav Klaus and parliament, where the opposition Social Democrats hold key positions.
Tensions between the three party coalition and the Social Democrats have heightened in recent days as campaigning gets underway for Senate elections scheduled for next month.
The Czech trade deficit hit a record 100.9 billion crowns for the January-August period, nearly double the 59.5 billion crown shortfall for the same period last year.

After the release of the eight month figures, Klaus called a meeting of top economic ministers including Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, Agriculture Minister Josef Lux, Tosovsky and head of the Czech Statistical Bureau Edvard Outrata to discuss the problem.
